question: It has been proved that the dissolution speed of the solvate that is formed when the griseofulvin and the chloroform are associated, is:

options.opa: Less than the unsolvated form of the drug.
options.opb: Limiting step of the disintegration of the tablets in which the drug is formulated.
options.opc: Greater than the unsolvated form of the drug.
options.opd: Limiting factor of the distribution of the drug to the aqueous sectors of the organism.
options.ope: Same as the unsolvated form of the drug.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Griseofulvin associates with chloroform -> Formation of solvate -> Increased dissolution speed compared to unsolvated form -> Greater dissolution rate -> opc. Greater than the unsolvated form of the drug. -> 80%

CHAIN: Griseofulvin formulated in tablets -> Disintegration of tablets -> Solvate dissolution speed affects tablet disintegration -> Solvate dissolution speed is the limiting step -> opb. Limiting step of the disintegration of the tablets in which the drug is formulated. -> 85%
enhanced_information: Griseofulvin associated with chloroform forms a solvate, increasing dissolution speed compared to the unsolvated form. This increased dissolution rate makes the solvate dissolution speed greater than the unsolvated form of the drug, supporting option opc. Additionally, the solvate dissolution speed is the limiting step in the disintegration of tablets containing the drug, aligning with option opb.
analysis: Based on the known medical knowledge, the dissolution speed of the solvate formed when griseofulvin and chloroform are associated is typically greater than the unsolvated form of the drug. This is a common phenomenon where solvated forms of drugs often exhibit higher dissolution rates compared to their unsolvated counterparts.
